record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.context_brief: membership of structured languages in DLOG
record.original_question: Given a language L that is already known to be accepted by a two-way deterministic pushdown automaton, or by a one-way nondeterministic counter machine, can one decide whether L also belongs to DLOG, the deterministic logarithmic-space class?

evidence.quote: (1) Does a given 2dpda-language (lnc-language), L, belong to DLOG?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A two-way deterministic pushdown automaton (2DPDA) is a deterministic pushdown automaton whose input head can move left, right, or stay, on a read-only input tape with end markers, and which accepts by entering a designated accepting state. A one-way nondeterministic counter machine (1NCM) is a one-way nondeterministic finite automaton equipped with a single integer counter that can be incremented, decremented, and tested for zero. Let DLOG denote the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine using O(log n) work-tape space.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input a description of either a 2DPDA M or a 1NCM N (accepting a language L), decides whether L ∈ DLOG?

Equivalently, is the membership problem "L(M) ∈ DLOG?" decidable on the class of 2DPDA descriptions, and is the analogous problem decidable on the class of 1NCM descriptions?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not yield a definitive resolution. While the equivalence problem for one-way DPDA was famously settled by Sénizergues, no source located confirms either decidability or undecidability of the question whether a given 2DPDA-language (or 1NCM-language) lies in DLOG. Most properties of this kind for 2DPDA/counter machines are known to be undecidable, but a specific resolution of this DLOG-membership question was not found in the search results.

status_evidence.title: L (complexity) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: L (LOGSPACE) is the class of decision problems solvable by a deterministic Turing machine using O(log n) space.
status_evidence.claim: Defines DLOG/L used in the problem statement; does not address decidability of membership for 2DPDA languages.

status_evidence.title: Two-Way Automata versus Logarithmic Space — Kapoutsis
status_evidence.snippet: Survey relating two-way automata models to logarithmic-space complexity classes.
status_evidence.claim: Studies relationships between two-way automata and DLOG but does not give a decision procedure for 2DPDA-language membership in DLOG.

status_evidence.title: Decidability of DPDA Language Equivalence via First-Order Grammars
status_evidence.snippet: Equivalence of one-way DPDA is decidable.
status_evidence.claim: Related decidability result on DPDA, but distinct from the DLOG-membership question for 2DPDA/1NCM.
